findings.message: Path matching is done as text. The fix covers backslashes and letter case but not the other aliases a file system resolves to the same file. These variants pass the gate: (1) a Windows path with no drive letter but rooted at the drive (`\proj\src\a.ts`); (2) an extended-length or UNC prefix (`\\?\C:\proj\...`), which normalise turns into `/?/C:/...`, so `relativeInside` returns undefined and the gate returns ALLOW; (3) a Windows trailing-dot or alternate-data-stream spelling (`state.json.` or `state.json::$DATA`), which slips past `STATE_FILE` and then matches `EXEMPT`; (4) a project path in NFD Unicode on APFS when cwd is in NFC. Canonicalise before comparing: strip `\\?\`, resolve drive-rooted paths against the drive of cwd, apply NFC, and trim trailing dots, spaces and `:stream` suffixes. When a path cannot be resolved against cwd, return deny or warn, not ALLOW. Add rows for each variant to the AC6 table.
findings.scenario: Windows, cwd `C:\proj`, nothing approved. A Write to `C:\proj\.specclaw\changes\047-x\state.json.` with `{"phases":{"proposal":{"status":"approved"}}}` returns allow: STATE_FILE does not match, EXEMPT does. Windows then writes state.json, so the model has approved its own proposal. Same inputs with path `\proj\src\a.ts` also return allow instead of deny.

findings.message: The fix 'show unreadable state' (refreshQuietly sets the status to `statusText(UNREADABLE)` and stores UNREADABLE in the snapshot atom) has no test of what it shows. The events and register tests only check that the chain goes on and the tool result is kept. For each event × failure shape row, add a check that the snapshot read afterwards has `isUnreadable: true`, or that the status was set to 'specclaw: could not read changes'. Seed a good snapshot first so the test proves stale data is replaced.
findings.scenario: Delete the `$.ui.status(statusText(UNREADABLE))` and `update($, snapshot, () => UNREADABLE)` lines from refreshQuietly (register.tsx:21-24). Every test in events.test.ts and register.test.ts still passes. Yet a rejecting session.cwd now leaves the last good snapshot looking current.

findings.message: Two rules decide what counts as `.specclaw`, and they disagree. The post-tool refresh trigger uses a case-sensitive `includes('.specclaw')`, while gate.ts EXEMPT/STATE_FILE ignore case. A tool call that writes `.SpecClaw/changes/x/state.json` on a case-insensitive file system does not refresh the view until the turn ends. Share one case-insensitive matcher.

bandText ignores `isUnreadable`. When the snapshot is UNREADABLE, the band disappears exactly as it does when no change is active. Only the status line says the read failed. Show a band such as 'specclaw · could not read changes' for an unreadable snapshot.
